newsitem.title: UK: LG Metals operating as normal - MG official.
newsitem.headline: LG Metals operating as normal - MG official.

text.p: Korea's LG Metals Corp has been trading with Germany's Metallgesellschaft AG (MG) as usual and there have been no signs of problems as rumoured in the market, an official of MG's London-based metals subsidiary said on Monday.
"They are customers of ours and we have a good relationship," Christian Schirmeister, Associate Director for Client Liason at MG unit Metallgesellschaft Ltd, told Reuters in an interview.

LG Futures Co Ltd, an affiliate of the LG Group, was asked last month by the Korean Finance Ministry to explain why its metals trade has surged this year. The firm has consistently denied rumours that it is facing huge option-related losses.
During a wide-ranging interview on metals markets, Schirmeister was asked whether the market had grounds for concern about LG.

He replied: "Absolutely not...From this point of the business, what I can see, what I can monitor, they haven't changed their way of trading, there was nothing extraordinary involved or any measures to be taken."

Schirmeister said the volume of trading by LG had expanded this year but the firm is a producer and told MG it was now hedging more of its output. It was unreasonable to grill a client on whether all trades were backed up by physical business.
"I can't ask my customer, 'Say, these 10 lots, against what physical deal is this?'," he said.

"They are an important, big user of the metal market by definition....We treat them like any other grade A, first class customer...we haven't changed our attitude towards them, there was no reason at all."
